newsitem.title: USA: United States not ready to take part in Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: United States not ready to take part in Zaire force.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it was not ready to take part in a multinational force proposed by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to aid refugees caught up in fighting in eastern Zaire.
"We're not ready to make a commitment to a multinational force at this time. We don't think the time is right to make that decision," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
Annan, encouraged by France, said last Friday in Paris that he hoped to persuade U.N. member states to revive the multinational force plan.

The plan collapsed last year when many of an estimated 1.2 million refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi returned home of their own accord. But more than 200,000 refugees remain trapped in Zaire.

The United States on Tuesday appealed to Laurent Kabila, leader of the Tutsi rebels fighting Zaire government forces in the region, to open corridors to allow the remaining refugees to leave the country.
"We'd rather wait and see how that operation goes ... before we entertain seriously the deployment of a multinational force to Zaire," Burns told reporters.
He said Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and other U.S. officials had discussed the force plan with Annan last weekend.

Burns implicitly criticised Zaire for expelling U.N. aid workers who had been in the region. "The Zairean government should have an interest in having those relief workers stay in Zaire, given the enormous problems there," he said.

The United States on Wednesday urged Americans to postpone any plans to travel to eastern Zaire, because of the fighting there. Burns said he believed most U.S. citizens who had been in the region had now left.

The Tutsi rebels took up arms last October when authorities tried to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda, and have seized a vast stretch of eastern Zaire with seemingly little resistance by Zaire's army.
